reviewer: A, Codex technical reviewer; independent of the drafting and typesetting of these texts
scope: Diff-only confirmation of all 19 supplied DE/EN fields in five items

findings.reason: Both sentence breaks after D and the English phrase 3 m up repair the stated slips. The one right, three up displacement is the same. The rubric preserves the half-mark deduction at its origin, the consequence rule, the cap and the 10/12 pass mark.

Both prompts give the same ordered components, now as columns. Reading rows from top to bottom gives magnitudes 5, 5 and 10. The sums remain (0,8) and (9,12), giving 8 < 10 and 15 = 15. Both geometric equality cases, marks, cap and follow-through survive in both languages.

The positive-x counterclockwise convention and open upper bound at 360 degrees are identical in both texts. At 150 degrees the components are still minus two times square root of three and positive two. For the column with entries -3 and -4 the same acute reference angle gives 233.1 degrees. The zero vector has no direction angle. Calculator, rounding allowance and 9/11 mark remain.
All four field changes re-express negative one half as the same signed fraction. Multiplication of both components, reversed direction and halved length of a nonzero arrow are identical.

Both languages keep r as magnitude, alpha counterclockwise from positive x, cosine for x, sine for y, quadrant signs and the undefined zero-vector direction. The new dollar delimiters and TeX names change only mathematical typography.
